chapter: Growing up with music in Austin
title: The Moonlight Serenaders social club band
summary: Teenage social clubs hired bands, so Ramey's Moonlight Serenaders, led by Carl Downs, formed their own dance band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well, when you -- you played the tuba in the high school, too, did you?
No, there wasn't anything in high school, no band at that time in high school.
Oh. Well, when did you play this?
Now, that's a round-about story. We -- as I said, we had clubs and things. I mean, they had parties things.
But where was it you got this sort of tuition?

We organized a club. There were other clubs; my club was the Moonlight Serenaders. And there was -- I had to write these names down, because I didn't remember them, too well. One of them was the Wild Fire Sheiks, and
Mine was Moonlight Serenaders. So now, we would take turns in giving dances. Sometimes we'd give dances on the same --

No, these were social clubs. We would hire little three or four pieces people to play for this thing for all us little teenagers, for the dance. And then somebody struck up on the idea that we're paying too much money for -- we're paying all this money out to the musicians; let's get our own band.

So then we organized -- we took money out of the -- what's its name -- and bought instruments for us. And you might have heard of Carl Downs (PHONETIC) who was the head of the Negro Fund for Colleges, for college students? (ed.-United Negro College Fund)

Well now, he was the leader of our group. We were all kids then, you know, but he later became that. And he was a trumpeter, and we made him president of our club. And then we had another trumpet player, clarinet player, and banjo, bass drum and piano. And so we'd play for the thing.
Well, we naturally became the most popular club, because first of all, we could provide more music. We would have five pieces or six pieces, where the other groups could
: But this band was a dance band?

Yeah, we formed it as a dance band. And we learned those things like "The Moon Comes Over the Mountain," and "Carolina Moon," and which is that "Farewell to Thee." Every blues that Mamie and Bessie and all of them sang, we had those down, you know. One of the guys sang, the piano player sang in the group. And so we -- that really started -- got me interested.
